name: Manitoba
summary_text: No province-specific trans law, incident series or official statement was found; federal criminal and human-rights law apply uniformly. Police-reported hate crime across all motivations sits at the national low (5.3 per 100,000 in 2024, tied with Newfoundland and Labrador). The province's 2021 gender-related homicide rate of women and girls (0.72 per 100,000, a Statistics Canada proxy) is mid-range and not trans-specific. Winnipeg hosts the organised provincial community. Risk assessed at parity with the national picture.

sources.title: The Daily — Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024
sources.claim_summary: Statistics Canada's release "Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024" (30 Mar 2026): 4,882 hate crimes reported nationally, +1% over 2023 (rate 11.9 per 100,000, -2%); incidents targeting gender identity or expression rose for a fourth consecutive year, +8% to 139 (nearly tripled, +184%, since 2020), and of known specific motivations more than half (56 of 98) targeted intersex, transgender, agender or non-binary people; sexual-orientation-motivated crimes fell 26% to 658 but remain above pre-2023 levels, with June (Pride season) running about twice the monthly average. National series - the release shows no trans-specific provincial pattern for this division.
